subtopics.title: What a GIS Is — Layers of Information

questions.question: A GIS is best defined as a computerised system that:
options: Takes photographs of the earth from space
Captures, stores, analyses, manages and displays geographically referenced information
Prints paper maps only
Measures rainfall automatically

questions.question: A list of hospital names becomes geographical information a GIS can use when:
options: It is typed into a computer
It is printed on a large map
Coordinates are attached to each hospital, georeferencing every record
The hospitals are sorted alphabetically

questions.question: Overlay analysis means:
options: Stacking georeferenced layers over the same ground and answering questions across them, such as where dense population lies far from any school
Drawing one very detailed map by hand
Printing two maps on one sheet of paper
Colouring a map with transparent inks

questions.question: For a hospital in a GIS, the number of beds and presence of a trauma unit are:
options: Spatial data
A separate layer
Coordinates
Attribute data

subtopics.title: The Five Components of a GIS

questions.question: The five components of a GIS are:
options: Hardware, software, data, people and procedures
Maps, satellites, planes, cameras and screens
Latitude, longitude, scale, legend and title
Input, output, memory, screen and printer

questions.question: Data is ranked the most valuable and most costly component because:
options: It is stored on the most expensive computers
Without accurate, current georeferenced data, the best hardware and software produce rubbish
It is protected by law
It takes up the most disk space

questions.question: The PROCEDURES component of a GIS covers:
options: The physical cables connecting the computers
The salaries of the analysts
Working rules — update schedules, accuracy checks, and records of who changed what
The programs that draw the maps

questions.question: In the engine summary of the five components, PEOPLE are described as:
options: The fuel
The service manual
The engine
The ones who steer — the system computes, humans conclude

questions.question: Remote sensing is defined as:
options: Collecting information about the earth's surface from a distance, without physical contact
Surveying land with measuring tapes
Interviewing households by telephone
Drawing maps from memory

questions.question: Remote sensors can reveal crop stress before any wilting is visible because:
options: They photograph at night
They fly very close to the crops
They read wavelengths beyond human vision, such as infrared, in the reflected energy
They water the crops while imaging them

questions.question: Compared with aerial photographs, satellite images:
options: Show finer detail over smaller areas
Cover enormous areas and revisit the same ground on a fixed schedule, building a time series
Are only available in black and white
Cannot be loaded into a GIS

questions.question: A key limit of remote sensing for population studies is that:
options: Satellites cannot photograph cities
Images never need interpretation
It is more expensive than visiting every household
A sensor counts structures like roofs but cannot learn residents' ages, language or employment — the ground census stays irreplaceable

subtopics.title: Satellites, Aerial Photographs and Population Work

questions.question: Satellite images taken months apart help metros like Ekurhuleni and Buffalo City by:
options: Revealing new roof clusters on the informal fringe, which become a GIS layer overlaid with water, sanitation and clinic layers
Counting the exact number of residents in each shack
Replacing the need for any municipal planning
Measuring household incomes from orbit

questions.question: Before a census, Statistics South Africa uses aerial and satellite imagery to:
options: Estimate the population so no counting is needed
Divide the country into small enumeration areas and ensure every dwelling appears on an enumerator's map
Photograph each household's identity documents
Broadcast the census questions

questions.question: During the June 2017 Knysna fires, remote sensing helped by:
options: Extinguishing the fires from orbit
Predicting the fires a year in advance
Mapping burn scars and destroyed neighbourhoods from before-and-after images while roads were still closed
Replacing the fire brigade

questions.question: SANSA's Hartebeesthoek station and the nanosatellite ZACube-2 show that South Africa:
options: Has no space capacity of its own
Only buys foreign maps
Uses satellites solely for television
Receives and distributes satellite data and builds its own earth-observation satellites

subtopics.title: The Smartphone Map You Already Use

questions.question: Searching for an open pharmacy on a phone counts as running a GIS because the app:
options: Captures, stores, analyses and displays georeferenced information about you and the pharmacies
Makes a phone call to the pharmacy
Uses the camera to photograph the street
Stores your search history

questions.question: In the pharmacy search, the map application itself is the component called:
options: Hardware
Software
Procedures
Data

questions.question: The pharmacy's pin on the map versus its name and opening hours illustrates:
options: Hardware versus software
Satellite versus aerial imagery
Spatial data (where it is) versus attribute data (what it is)
Raster versus paper maps

questions.question: In the tracing paper picture, one sheet with only the district's rivers on it represents:
options: A GIS layer — one theme, georeferenced to the same ground as the others
An attribute table
A GPS receiver
A satellite image

questions.question: Pressing the aligned stack against the light exposes, for example:
options: The names of the district's residents
The age of each map sheet
The cost of drawing the maps
Crowded homesteads with no school nearby, and homesteads standing inside a floodplain

questions.question: If the school layer is six years out of date, the GIS analysis:
options: Automatically corrects itself
May demand a school where one already stands — a GIS makes stale data look authoritative, never true
Refuses to run
Deletes the old layer

subtopics.title: The Eye in the Sky and the Census

questions.question: Playing satellite images of Theewaterskloof Dam in date order during the Cape drought showed:
options: The dam's water line creeping backwards month by month — change detected through repeat imaging
The number of people using the dam
The temperature of the water only
Nothing, because dams cannot be imaged

questions.question: South Africa's 1 to 10 000 orthophoto maps are built from:
options: Hand-drawn sketches
Weather radar
Corrected aerial photographs, detailed enough to show single rooftops
Ship-based surveys

questions.question: Healthy and struggling maize can be told apart from orbit because:
options: Struggling maize is always shorter
Satellites hover directly above each field
Farmers paint their healthy fields
Thriving plants blaze in infrared while struggling plants dim — wavelengths sensors read but eyes cannot

questions.question: "The satellite counts roofs, never people" means:
options: Satellites cannot see roofs clearly
Remote sensing shows where dwellings are, but only a person at the door can learn who lives there — so census fieldwork remains essential
Roofs block all satellite signals
Counting people from space is illegal
